question: Can past observed motion predict a change in annotated exit target within the next two seconds?
scope: Low-pressure autonomous pedestrian egress; camera-observation prediction, not guidance causality or fire-control validation.
sample_policy: Every eligible track: first_frame+history_frames, then stride_frames; retain unchanged tracks and all eligible windows.
time_policy: Preserve raw frames. Cross-person synchronized snapshots remain disabled until the common camera clock is verified. Individual first-frame elapsed seconds only for track-relative diagnostics. Do not equate first-frame time with acoustic start.
privileged_annotation_condition: Separate secondary condition. If current/past annotated target is supplied, supply it equally to all methods and disclose retrospective annotation.
split_disclosure: Structural counts/labels have already been audited across all runs. Proposed partition is not wholly unseen data, and repeated-participant independence is unverified. Freeze before predictive evaluation; do not move runs after seeing model scores.
baselines: maintain inferred route (requires validated map for exit probabilities)
regularized dynamic Logit using exactly the same observed features
one locked local LLM using exactly the same feature serialization
aggregation: Report per-run results and both run-macro and person-run-macro averages. Windows are repeated measurements. Bootstrap runs only as exploratory sensitivity; cannot remove unknown across-run person dependence.
rare_event_rule: Do not claim success from overall accuracy. Report event/person-run/window denominators separately. Case-control samples, if used for low-cost LLM diagnosis, are secondary and cannot yield population precision without design correction.
decision_rule: After map and semantics preflight, run a bounded baseline pilot. Start one LLM comparison only if protocol and model settings are locked. Do not resume PPO from a behavior-prediction score alone.
